title: Quantization fidelity strata benchmarking and regression guard-harness
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reproducible harness that evaluates FP16/INT8/INT4 quantization profiles across representative workloads, tracks throughput (tokens/sec) and latency p95, and detects quality regressions using composite metrics. The harness should support multiworkload composition, synthetic replay from production traces, and automated statistical regression alerts that feed into CI and the Console QA dashboard.
rationale: Existing quant sweeps are ad-hoc and focus on single-metric outputs (throughput or accuracy). We need a repeatable, signal-rich harness that exposes tradeoffs between unit cost and output fidelity, and that can block regressions introduced by kernel, scheduler, or quantization parameter changes.
approach: Create a modular runner that: 1) executes workload profiles (chat, generation, embeddings, long-context) against model+quant variants, 2) collects tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, and memory pressure, 3) evaluates quality via reference prompt sets (instruction-following, factuality, embedding similarity), 4) computes composite score (perf-normalized fidelity), and 5) triggers regression detection using configurable baselines and statistical tests (paired bootstrap / t-test + effect size). Integrate with perf CI, Console dashboards, and daily regression monitors.
metrics: tokens_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tail99_latency_ms, GPU_util_pct, mem_peak_mb, token_cost_estimate, fidelity_score (0-1), embed_cosine_mean, rouge_l, instruction_pass_rate
test_matrix: Models: open-gpt-family-7B, open-gpt-family-13B; Quant profiles: FP16 (baseline), INT8, INT8+KV-cache-preserve, INT4 per-layer hybrid; Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16; Sequence lengths: 64, 512, 2048; Workloads: chat (multi-turn), single-turn completion, streaming response, embeddings; Load shapes: steady (sustained qps), burst (spike), sawtooth (ramping).
quality_checks: Reference prompt sets (1000 prompts per workload) with ground-truth outputs / human-annotated labels. Automated scoring: embedding cosine threshold, rouge_l delta, instruction-follow pass/fail classifiers. Define fidelity_score = weighted combination of normalized metrics. Regression threshold = 3% absolute drop in fidelity_score OR statistically significant (p<0.01) degradation with effect size > 0.2.
regression_detection: Nightly baseline runs produce per-profile baselines. New runs compared to baseline use paired bootstrap to produce confidence intervals and p-values. Alerts: Slack alert to #eng-quant and create Linear ticket when threshold crossed. CI gating: any PR that causes mean tokens/sec drop >5% at p95 latency increase >10% or fidelity drop >2% is flagged as failing benchmark gate.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end for all combinations in test_matrix and produces reproducible JSON artifacts with metrics and per-prompt quality scores.
Automated regression detection produces alerts and creates Linear tickets when thresholds breached.
Perf CI integration: PRs can reference a benchmark run; benchmark job returns pass/fail status based on defined gates.
Console dashboard shows tokens/sec and p95 trends per quant profile, and a fidelity_vs_cost scatter view for all experiments.
At least one regression detection test has caught an intentional synthetic degradation injected for verification.
Documentation and runbook for how to add new model or workload profiles.
Unit and integration tests for statistical comparison code (coverage > 85%).
implementation_steps: Design JSON schema for run artifacts (per-prompt results and aggregated summary).
Implement workload runner module with pluggable backends (hosted API + local runtime test harness).
Wire metric collectors: latency histograms, tokens/sec counters, GPU exporter hooks.
Implement quality scoring pipelines: embedding similarity, rouge, instruction pass classifier.
Add regression detection library (paired bootstrap + reporting).
Add Grafana dashboards and Console integration points.
Create CI job and PR gating logic; add test that injects synthetic regression for verification.
Run initial sweep across 2 models and 4 quant profiles; publish results and short writeup.
risks: Measurement noise on short runs can produce false positives; production traces have privacy constraints requiring sanitization; some quant profiles are non-deterministic across runs (seed drift) which complicates paired comparisons.
mitigations: Use long runs or replicate runs (n>=5) for statistical power, use sanitized and anonymized production-replay traces, enforce deterministic seeds where possible, and compute effect sizes to avoid overreacting to tiny absolute deltas.
notes: Prefer to leverage existing quant-bench repo; close collaboration with Applied ML for prompt set selection; coordinate with Console team for dashboard wiring and RBAC of benchmark results.
